title: CDSCO Expert Panel Recommends Late-Phase Trials of Two Haemophilia Drugs

contentHtml:
New Delhi: India's apex drug regulator, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), through its Subject Expert Committee (SEC) on Haematology, has recommended allowing Novo Nordisk to conduct a Phase IIIb clinical trial of denecimig and Pfizer to proceed with a Phase III trial of marstacimab in India, advancing the evaluation of two investigational therapies for haemophilia.

The recommendations were made during the SEC meeting held on November 17, 2026, under the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), India's apex drug regulatory authority.

For Novo Nordisk's denecimig, the committee's recommendation came after the company submitted a revised clinical trial protocol along with additional information sought by the panel. The SEC had previously requested clarifications in July regarding the proposed clinical trial involving patients with acquired haemophilia A (AHA).

Following the submission of the revised protocol and additional details, the committee reviewed the proposal and recommended that Novo Nordisk be allowed to conduct a Phase IIIb clinical trial of denecimig.

Separately, the committee recommended that Pfizer proceed with a Phase III clinical trial of marstacimab for haemophilia. Both candidates are non-factor therapies being developed for the treatment of the bleeding disorder.

The proposed clinical trials could contribute to the development of additional treatment approaches for haemophilia patients. However, the availability of newer therapies does not eliminate existing challenges in accessing treatment. High therapy costs and shortages of essential medicines continue to restrict access for patients.

According to Business Standard, the CDSCO's Subject Expert Committee on Haematology recommended the two clinical trials at its November 17 meeting, following its review of the proposals and the additional information submitted by the companies.

The recommendations represent a step forward in the clinical development of denecimig and marstacimab in India, with both therapies requiring further clinical evaluation.
